Somerville.narrative: Somerville's real estate market is operating at a fever pitch across all property types, with single families closing at a median of $1.15M, condos at $985K, and multi-families leading the pack at $1.238M — all with essentially zero months of supply, signaling an extremely inventory-starved environment. Competition is fierce, with nearly half of all condos (46.4%) and multi-families (45.5%) selling above asking price, and even single families hitting their list price exactly at a 100% SP/LP ratio with a third of homes going over ask. For sellers, conditions couldn't be more favorable — properly priced homes are generating multiple offers almost immediately, and those with multi-families in particular are seeing strong investor and house-hacker demand driving premiums. Buyers should come prepared with pre-approvals locked, escalation clauses ready, and realistic expectations that in Somerville's hyper-competitive market, the asking price is often just the starting point of the conversation.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of the most competitive markets in Greater Boston, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $2,595,000 and an extraordinary 104% sale-to-list ratio, as nearly two-thirds of all single-family sales closed above asking price over the past 30 days. The condo market, while more accessible at a $929,500 median, is equally tight with 71 units sold in 30 days and a full 100% sale-to-list ratio, meaning buyers should expect little to no negotiating leverage and must come in strong from the start. Multi-family properties are also holding firm near $2.17M with 99.7% of list price achieved, reflecting sustained investor and owner-occupant demand across all asset classes. With effectively zero months of supply across the board, sellers are in an exceptionally powerful position right now, while buyers should be prepared to waive contingencies, move quickly, and work with a lender who can close fast to stay competitive in this supply-starved Cambridge market.

Medford.narrative: Medford's housing market remains intensely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $887,500 and an impressive 102.2% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely paying above asking, as evidenced by 57.1% of single-family sales closing over list price. Condos offer a comparatively accessible entry point at a $609,500 median, though even that segment sees 25% of units selling above ask, while multi-family properties command a hefty $1,125,000 median with half of all sales exceeding list price. With no measurable months of supply across all three categories and only 28 total transactions in the past 30 days, inventory is essentially nonexistent, signaling an acutely supply-constrained market. Sellers are in an exceptionally strong position to attract multiple offers and premium pricing, while buyers should expect to move fast, come in above ask, and keep contingencies lean to stay competitive in one of Metro Boston's tightest submarkets.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose remains a fiercely competitive market across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $985,000 and an eye-popping 109.2% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely paying nearly 10% above asking, with 81% of homes selling over list price in the past 30 days. Multi-families are also commanding serious attention at a $1,341,000 median, while condos offer a comparatively accessible entry point at $301,250, though even that segment sees half of units closing above asking. With effectively zero months of supply across all categories and only 21 single-family sales recorded in the last 30 days, inventory is critically tight, giving sellers enormous leverage and the realistic expectation of multiple offers and quick closings. For buyers, Melrose demands aggressive preparation — strong pre-approvals, escalation clauses, and limited contingencies are essentially table stakes in this environment.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $1,400,000 and an eye-popping 104.1% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely bidding well above asking, with 76.5% of single-family sales closing over list price in the last 30 days. Condos are holding strong at a $868,000 median with 45.5% of units selling over ask, while multi-families are trading at $1,175,000 with half of all sales exceeding list price. With effectively zero months of supply across all three categories and only 45 total transactions closed in the past 30 days, inventory is critically tight, creating an environment where well-priced homes are generating immediate multiple-offer situations. For sellers, this is an exceptional moment to capitalize on premium pricing and fast closings, while buyers should come prepared with pre-approvals, escalation clauses, and the flexibility to waive contingencies in order to compete effectively in one of Metro Boston's most in-demand suburbs.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with essentially zero months of supply signaling near-total inventory exhaustion. Single-family homes are leading the charge with a median sale price of $1,558,500, 75% of properties selling above asking price, and a sale-to-list ratio of 103.4%, while multi-family properties are actually seeing the most aggressive bidding at 108.7% of list price with that same 75% over-ask rate on just 4 sales in the past 30 days. Condos offer a comparatively softer entry point at a $750,000 median with only 20% selling over ask and a 99.0% SP/LP ratio, though "softer" is relative in a town with no available supply. For buyers, Belmont demands strong pre-approval, aggressive offer strategies, and a willingness to waive contingencies, while sellers across all property classes are in an exceptional position to command premium pricing with minimal days on market.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $1,075,000 and an eye-catching 101.7% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely paying above asking, with fully two-thirds of homes selling over list price. Condos offer a relatively more accessible entry point at a $677,500 median, though even there nearly 28% of units are trading above ask at a 98.9% SP/LP ratio, signaling strong demand at every price tier. Multi-family properties are commanding a hefty $1,325,000 median with all sales hitting or exceeding list price, making them attractive investment vehicles but increasingly difficult to pencil out for first-time investors. With inventory so thin that months of supply is essentially nonexistent across the board, sellers hold significant leverage right now — while buyers should come prepared with strong pre-approvals, flexible terms, and the expectation that list price is really just the starting point.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's single-family market is commanding serious attention, with a median sale price of $1,850,000 and homes closing at 97.1% of list price — 35.3% of them selling above asking — signaling that well-priced properties are generating strong competition despite elevated price points. The condo segment may actually be the hotter story, with a median of $805,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 100.2%, and a remarkable 66.7% of units closing over ask, meaning buyers in that price range should expect bidding wars as the norm rather than the exception. With 17 single-family and 9 condo sales in the past 30 days and essentially no measurable months of supply across all property types, inventory is critically tight — a decisive win for sellers who can expect swift, competitive offers. Buyers entering Winchester right now need to come prepared with strong financials, minimal contingencies, and realistic expectations that list price is often just the starting point.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single families commanding a median of $919,500 and selling at exactly list price with over half — 53.1% — closing above asking, while multifamilies lead on price at $1,125,000 with nearly 45% of sales topping list price. The condo market is the most active segment with 347 sales in the past 30 days at a median of $825,000, and even that traditionally more buyer-friendly category saw 30.5% of units sell over ask at a 99.3% sale-to-list ratio. With months of supply data effectively at zero across all three property types, inventory is critically tight, signaling that Boston is operating in one of the most constrained markets in recent memory. Sellers are in an exceptionally strong position with little competition and consistent full-price or above offers, while buyers should expect to move fast, come in at or above list, and have financing airtight before stepping through the door.
